USA.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Maintain the proposed Section 301 tariffs as leverage but do not escalate into an all-out trade war — open and pursue bilateral negotiations with China while the tariffs remain unimposed. Keep the ~$50B list and any further threats on the table as bargaining chips to force real changes to China's IP and technology-transfer practices, but halt the march toward a $100B+ across-the-board confrontation that would hit US markets and the farm belt. Use the public-comment window (through May 22) and China's stated openness to talks to push for structural concessions before any tariffs take effect.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat to US interests is moderate, not existential. The US initiated this dispute over genuine grievances (China's forced technology transfer and IP theft, per the USTR Section 301 findings and fact sheet) and holds leverage — the tariffs are still proposed, with a comment period through May and a hearing on May 15, so nothing has been imposed yet (Steptoe). The US economy is fundamentally healthy: industrial production rose to ~103 and consumer sentiment held near 98.8-101, with no recession signal (country_health INDPRO, UMCSENT). That said, the dispute carries real bite: China's retaliatory ~$50B proposal (entry 2018-04-04) explicitly targets soybeans, autos, and aircraft — striking the farm belt that delivered Trump his electoral base and causing sharp overnight market and soybean-futures declines and heavy lobbying by farm groups and farm-state Republicans (web: CNBC/LA Times/Business Insider). This mix of solid fundamentals, US-held leverage, but genuine domestic-export and political exposure justifies a mid-single-digit-positive threat (~+0.3). On action, escalation to maximal $100B tariffs would risk an uncontrolled trade war that damages US consumers, supply chains, and the president's own political base, while full concession now would forfeit hard-won leverage before China has made a matching offer. The disciplined path is to hold the tariff threat steady and negotiate — a slight-negative action score (~-0.1) consistent with 'negotiate', reflecting firmness without new commitments and without capitulation.
key_factors: US holds the initiative and leverage (Section 301 on China's IP/forced tech transfer); tariffs still proposed, not imposed, with a comment window through May 22
US macro is sound (industrial production rising, sentiment ~99) — no recession signal yet
China's ~$50B retaliatory proposal targets the soybean/auto/aircraft export sectors — direct hit to Trump's farm-belt base
Markets and soybean futures plunged on retaliation fears; farm groups and farm-state Republicans pressed for de-escalation
Escalating to a $100B all-out trade war would harm US consumers, supply chains, and domestic politics before China has made concessions

sources_cited.excerpt: USTR publishes proposed Section 301 tariff list ~$50B
China announces proposed retaliatory tariffs on ~$50B of US goods including soybeans, automobiles, aircraft
Futures in stocks, soybeans and dollar tanked overnight on China's retaliation
None of the tariffs goes into effect immediately; comment period to May 22, providing ample time for negotiations
Soybeans are largest US agricultural export to China (~$14.6B); farm groups and Republican senators urge reconsideration
